title: GBE Autos — master product roadmap (single GBE platform and primary website, 2026-07-10)
consultation_summary: The authoritative consultation (docs/product/inputs/MASTER_PRODUCT_ROADMAP_CONSULTATION_20260710.md) directs a complete master product roadmap, not merely a stabilization plan. It reconciles the confirmed product-owner decisions (HUMAN_PRODUCT_DECISIONS_20260710.md), the verified live Supabase read-only audit (F002 remains partially captured), the existing single-site stabilization blueprint (docs/product/roadmaps/gbe-single-site-homepage-roadmap-20260710/), the AGIREAL reuse matrix, and the roadmap-alignment audit. Confirmed model: one GBE platform and one primary GBE public website; Payload stays the CMS/workflow/auth/API foundation; Supabase Postgres is the authoritative database and Supabase Storage the durable byte store; exactly three fail-closed roles (admin/general/sales); dealerships are inventory/location references with approved optional off-site links, never separate hosted sites; the primary homepage is the first major customer-facing priority; Spanish/Mexico behavior is the default. The alignment audit's multi-agency/tenant recommendations are explicitly rejected — no tenant feature exists, active or deferred — while its valid omissions are accepted as new mandatory workstreams: reproducible delivery foundation, authentication operations, inventory-first import/review workflow at ~1,400-vehicle scale, Builder V2 with a versioned block registry, a dedicated operator console outside the Payload Admin CSS boundary, a modern main GBE Storefront, a durable AI Media Studio, an inventory assistant with controlled agents, leads/WhatsApp sales workflow, trusted analytics with dealer-facing reporting, and shared contracts with a bounded monorepo decision. Sequencing corrections applied: a baseline CI slice precedes the critical role migration; the incomplete F002 live SQL capture blocks only the migrations that need its outputs; homepage builder mechanics may precede media reconciliation but public launch requires durable media; the final Storefront release gate depends on canonical durable media and legacy reconciliation; the obsolete tenant feature is removed from the active list and preserved only as a rejected decision; clean Admin and Storefront SHAs must be pinned before any implementation layer is approved.
product_outcome: GBE operates one trustworthy platform behind its primary public website: staff sign in under exactly three fail-closed roles and work in a dedicated operator console with a product-owned design system; inventory arrives through governed CSV/XLSX and agent-assisted imports with mapping, normalization, duplicate detection, dry run, human approval, idempotent commits, and rollback at ~1,400-vehicle scale; vehicle images and AI-generated media flow through durable Supabase Storage behind canonical Payload Media with provenance, moderation, budgets, and reviewer approval — never auto-published; the primary homepage and later pages are built in Builder V2 on a single versioned block registry with draft/preview/publish/unpublish/rollback and concurrency protection from site_config as the sole source of truth; the modern GBE Storefront renders those contracts with accurate navigation, complete deterministic catalog filters/sorts, trust and conversion modules, real 404s, SEO, and measurable performance; visitors convert through GBE-owned lead capture and dealership/city-aware WhatsApp handoff with approved off-site links as supplemental routing; sales staff manage leads in an inbox with assignment, stages, and response SLAs; and dealers read trusted analytics — bounded sessions, attribution, bot filtering, idempotent events, and rollups — while every release passes a pinned-SHA cross-repository gate proven by Node 22 CI.
repo_assessment: Live repository inspected at branch codex/admin-workflow-updates, HEAD d6d505f (plus uncommitted logo/custom.scss/vehicle-preview/launch-config edits and untracked docs, scripts, and src/utils/formatMileage.ts). All foundation findings of the preserved stabilization blueprint were re-confirmed: fail-open six-role model (src/access/roles.ts:12-40, live enum matches), no storage adapter (src/payload.config.ts plugins: [] with local uploads in src/collections/Media.ts), publish-on-save HomeBuilder against an unversioned SiteConfig global, text price and overlapping status/image fields on Vehicles, anonymous Leads/AnalyticsEvents creation, mounted raw REST/GraphQL beside bounded public DTO routes, no versions/drafts anywhere, no .github/workflows, and no test or typecheck script (package.json pins node 22.x). New master-roadmap evidence gathered this session: (1) Imports — a real but commit-only pipeline exists: src/app/(payload)/api/cms/import/run/route.ts creates vehicles as drafts with sourceId/stockId duplicate detection (:110-137) after client-side CSV/XLSX parsing in src/components/admin-ui/VehicleImportModal.tsx (:44-118); src/collections/ImportJobs.ts declares validating/ready/rolled_back statuses (:42-55) and createdVehicleIds (:82-87) that no code ever writes; there is no dry run, human approval, idempotency key, or rollback endpoint, and csv-parse is a declared but unused dependency. (2) Inventory operations — completeness scoring is computed on save (src/collections/Vehicles.ts:687-697 via src/services/vehicleWorkflow.ts:89-107) with publish gating (:358-363) and a triage view in src/components/views/InventoryManager.tsx, but no aging or exposure fields exist anywhere. (3) AI studio — durable DB-backed workshop jobs with chat, outputs, and approval states exist (src/collections/WorkshopJobs.ts:33-188); generation is a single blocking OpenRouter/Grok call (src/app/(payload)/api/cms/workshop/generate/route.ts:13-18,204-254) gated by ENABLE_AI_IMAGE_WIZARD (:286-296) with no queue, retry, timeout, cancellation, idempotency, cost ledger, quota, or moderation; outputs land in Payload Media (:379-395) and enter review as needs_review vehicle-media-assets (src/components/views/VehicleAIImageWizard.tsx:718-754); a complete reviewer-gated approve/reject/assign pipeline exists (src/app/(payload)/api/cms/vehicle-media-assets/review/route.ts, assign/route.ts; src/collections/VehicleMediaAssets.ts:69-84); the banner/promo/social MediaWorkspaceView/Manager is fully coded but registered nowhere (absent from src/payload.config.ts views and importMap.js) and therefore unreachable. (4) Leads/WhatsApp — src/collections/Leads.ts carries stage (:79-93) and assignment fields (:94-96) but no SLA, dedup, or UTM fields, with public create (:7-12); WhatsApp numbers are stored (src/globals/SiteConfig.ts:35,44; src/collections/Dealerships.ts:34) and a routing contract is validated at publish (src/collections/Vehicles.ts:645-652; src/services/vehicleWorkflow.ts:188-189; migration 20260610_100000_p0_whatsapp_routing_contracts.ts), but no wa.me link generation or lead inbox exists in this repo. (5) Analytics — src/collections/AnalyticsEvents.ts defines ten event types (:26-42) with plain sessionId/visitorId strings (:61-62), public create and authenticated-only update/delete (:5-10), no idempotency, UTM, consent, or bot filtering; src/components/AnalyticsDashboard.tsx reads raw events capped at 300 rows (:123-159); no rollup layer or dealer-scoped reporting exists. (6) Auth operations — Payload-default auth (src/collections/Users.ts:32), an admin-only invite route that reuses forgotPassword (src/app/(payload)/api/users/invite/route.ts:29-73), SMTP conditionally wired via nodemailer (src/payload.config.ts:129-143), no rate limiting anywhere and no middleware.ts. (7) Architecture — every operator surface lives inside Payload Admin as registered custom views (src/payload.config.ts:59-104) styled by one 8,722-line global custom.scss with zero CSS modules; shared primitives exist (src/components/admin-ui/kit.tsx, SectionBuilder.tsx at 1,218 lines, prompt-kit); public DTO types live only in src/services/publicVehicleCatalog.ts; 14 homepage block types are defined in src/blocks/SiteSections.ts wired to SiteConfig; there is no packages/ directory, workspace tooling, or block-schema drift check; the repository root redirects to /admin and the Storefront consumer is a separate repository absent from this workspace.

decisions_required.question: What is the exact permission matrix for the three target roles admin, general, and sales?
decisions_required.why: The confirmed model has exactly three roles, but capability today is spread across six legacy roles (src/access/roles.ts:60-86: canManageInventory, canManageContent, canManageMedia, MEDIA_REVIEW_ROLES, canManageLeads). Every collection access rule, field rule, custom route guard, import endpoint, media review gate, and AI studio gate must be rewritten against the approved matrix; engineering cannot infer which of general/sales inherits inventory, content, media review, or lead management.
options: Approve a written per-collection/per-operation matrix for admin, general, and sales before F001 implementation starts
Map general = all current non-admin operational capabilities and sales = lead/analytics management only, then refine after launch
Defer any capability change and only rename/collapse roles 1:1 (not recommended — leaves the matrix ambiguous)

decisions_required.question: What is the private per-user mapping of every existing user to admin, general, or sales?
decisions_required.why: The live enum is the legacy six-role set and public.users reports 3 rows with unknown per-user values (the aggregate SQL was cancelled). getRoles currently treats roleless users as admins (src/access/roles.ts:38), so the fail-closed migration must abort on unmapped users. The audit states no legacy role can be automatically mapped; this is a private human decision executed through a runbook, with identity-level output kept out of the audit trail.
options: Run the safe role-distribution capture, then privately review and sign off a mapping for every user before the migration
Default all three users to admin explicitly and downgrade later (ratifies over-privilege but preserves access)
Default unmapped users to no role (fail-closed immediately; risks locking out active staff)

decisions_required.question: Which legacy homepage content is retained in site_config: the registered site_config rows, the legacy home/home_stats/home_brands rows, or a hand-picked merge?
decisions_required.why: Both models contain live rows (MCP-live-verified), so making site_config the single source of truth requires a business content decision about what migrates before the legacy home family and unregistered src/globals/Home.ts are retired. options: Review both contents side by side and hand-pick what migrates into site_config before retiring the legacy family
Declare current site_config content canonical as-is and archive/drop the legacy rows after a backup export
Migrate everything from home into site_config mechanically and edit down afterwards

options: Pin the current Storefront main-branch SHA now, run F020 baseline capture early, and keep F017 as the final release gate
Accept Admin-side API contract tests as the acceptance boundary and defer Storefront verification (weakens the release gate; not recommended)

decisions_required.question: Who executes the blocked read-only SQL captures, and through which channel, to close F002?

Run the same SQL via the Supabase dashboard SQL editor read-only and archive sanitized outputs

decisions_required.question: Does vehicle presentation content live in a separate versioned related model (preferred) or directly on Vehicles?
decisions_required.why: Safe vehicle presentation editing is now a required capability, not optional — the open decision is only its shape. Presentation fields share the live vehicle record (src/collections/Vehicles.ts) with no versions config, so enabling Payload versions on Vehicles would version operational churn (inventoryStatus, publishStatus) together with marketing content. The consultation states separation is preferred and this decision must not block homepage work.
options: Extract presentation content into a separate versioned collection related to Vehicles (preferred)
Enable versions/drafts on Vehicles as-is and accept mixed inventory/content history

decisions_required.question: What is the primary conversion strategy: GBE lead form, dealership/city-aware WhatsApp handoff, approved off-site redirect — and what rules choose among them per vehicle/dealership/city?
decisions_required.why: The consultation keeps the exact balance a human conversion-strategy decision. The schema already stores WhatsApp numbers per site and dealership (src/globals/SiteConfig.ts:35,44; src/collections/Dealerships.ts:34) and validates routing completeness at publish (src/services/vehicleWorkflow.ts:188-189), but approved external links must remain supplemental routing, not an automatic replacement for GBE-owned measurable conversion flows — sending traffic off-site by default would bypass GBE's own lead and measurement system.
options: GBE lead form plus WhatsApp handoff as the primary journey everywhere; approved off-site links shown only as secondary options
WhatsApp-first with the GBE lead form as fallback; off-site links only where a dealership explicitly requests them
Per-dealership policy field deciding form/WhatsApp/redirect priority, with a platform default of GBE-owned capture

decisions_required.question: What route/deployment boundary hosts the dedicated operator console, and what is the migration cadence for moving workflows out of Payload Admin?
decisions_required.why: The console must live outside the stock Payload Admin layout and its 8,722-line global CSS boundary (src/app/(payload)/custom.scss). Candidate boundaries differ in operational cost: a new route group in this Next.js app, a separate app in the same repository, or a separately deployed application. The cadence decision controls how long the interim CSS containment (F016) must hold and which workflow migrates first.
options: New isolated route group (e.g. /console) inside this Next.js app with its own layout, design tokens, and zero Payload Admin CSS imports — lowest operational overhead
Separate app in the same repository (pending the D10 workspace decision) deployed independently
Separately hosted operator application consuming the same APIs (highest isolation, highest operational cost)

decisions_required.question: When does the shared-package/monorepo migration happen, and how far does it go?
decisions_required.why: Public DTOs, catalog options, block schemas, renderer expectations, and analytics event types currently live only inside this repository (src/services/publicVehicleCatalog.ts, src/blocks/SiteSections.ts) while the Storefront consumes them by convention. The consultation requires one source for these contracts and a bounded migration decision — but a large repository move must not block urgent security, homepage, or media fixes, and Admin/platform and Storefront must remain independently deployable.
options: Publish a versioned shared contracts package first (types, block schemas, fixtures) consumed by both repositories; defer any monorepo restructure until after launch
Adopt a workspace monorepo (Admin + Storefront + shared packages) at a scheduled point after the security and media milestones
Keep contracts in-repo and enforce parity with cross-repository drift checks only (lowest cost, weakest guarantee)

decisions_required.question: Which AI providers, budgets, quotas, moderation policy, and approval owners govern the AI Media Studio and agent features?
decisions_required.why: Generation currently calls OpenRouter with a Grok image model chosen by env default (src/app/(payload)/api/cms/workshop/generate/route.ts:13-18) with no cost ledger, quota, or moderation. The provider abstraction, cost reservation/ledger, per-role quotas, safety/moderation policy, and named approval owners are business commitments that must be decided before cost-bearing AI endpoints are hardened and exposed to the operator team.
options: Approve a provider list with monthly budget caps, per-user/per-role quotas, a moderation policy, and named approval owners before F030 implementation
Start with a single approved provider and conservative hard caps, expanding after the cost ledger proves spend visibility
Keep the AI studio behind its feature flag until a full provider/budget policy exists (delays capability G)

features.business_value: Closes the highest-leverage security hole — every guard currently fails open to admin for roleless authenticated users — and aligns the entire authorization layer with the confirmed three-role product model before any other feature builds on it.
